description: A local fact-and-question bank for a scored billiards trivia app, organized into 7 core topics with three difficulty tiers each.

facts.text: The cue ball is the only ball on the table without a number, and it's the one you strike with the cue stick.
A 'scratch' occurs when the cue ball is pocketed or forced off the table.
'Position play' is the practice of controlling where the cue ball stops after a shot, setting up the next shot in a sequence called a 'run.'

questions.question: What is a 'scratch' in billiards?
options: Pocketing the cue ball or knocking it off the table
Missing every ball on the table
questions.correctAnswer: Pocketing the cue ball or knocking it off the table
questions.explanation: A scratch is a foul where the cue ball itself ends up pocketed or leaves the table.

questions.question: What is 'position play'?
options: Racking the balls in a specific pattern
Controlling where the cue ball stops to set up the next shot
Standing in a specific spot at the table
questions.correctAnswer: Controlling where the cue ball stops to set up the next shot
questions.explanation: Skilled players plan not just the current shot but where the cue ball lands afterward.

questions.question: A sequence of consecutive pocketed balls without a miss is called a...?
questions.correctAnswer: Run
questions.explanation: A 'run' refers to consecutive successful shots, often tracked as a scoring statistic.

facts.text: The 8-ball is solid black and must be pocketed last in standard eight-ball.
Pocketing the 8-ball before clearing your group (solids or stripes) results in an automatic loss.
Under call-shot rules, a player must announce both the ball and the intended pocket before shooting at the 8-ball.

questions.question: What color is the 8-ball?
questions.correctAnswer: Black
questions.explanation: The 8-ball is solid black with a white number 8 on it.

questions.question: What happens if you pocket the 8-ball before clearing your group?
questions.correctAnswer: You lose the game
questions.explanation: Pocketing the 8-ball early is one of the most common instant-loss fouls in the game.

questions.question: In call-shot rules, what must a player announce before shooting the 8-ball?
options: Both the ball and the intended pocket
Nothing — the 8-ball never needs to be called
questions.correctAnswer: Both the ball and the intended pocket
questions.explanation: Call-shot rules require naming both which ball and which pocket for the 8-ball to count.

facts.text: Chalk is applied to the cue tip before a shot to increase friction and prevent miscues.
In call-shot games like straight pool or standard 8-ball, a player must verbally announce which ball and pocket they intend to hit.
Failing to properly call a bank shot, combination, or carom can turn a legal pot into a foul, even if the ball goes in.

questions.question: Why do players apply chalk to the cue tip?
options: To make the tip look nicer
To increase friction and prevent miscues
To make the cue ball curve more
questions.correctAnswer: To increase friction and prevent miscues
questions.explanation: Chalk keeps the tip from slipping off the ball, which would otherwise cause a miscue.

questions.question: In 'call-shot' games, what must a player do before attempting a shot?
options: Announce the object ball and pocket
questions.correctAnswer: Announce the object ball and pocket
questions.explanation: Call-shot rules require declaring intent so accidental pots don't count.

questions.question: What happens if a player pockets a ball via an uncalled bank or combination shot?
options: It's typically ruled a foul even though the ball went in
questions.correctAnswer: It's typically ruled a foul even though the ball went in
questions.explanation: Complex shots (banks, combos, caroms) usually must be explicitly called to count.

facts.text: Pool table felt is traditionally green, echoing billiards' origins as a lawn game played on grass.
A regulation tournament table is roughly twice as long as it is wide — e.g., 9 feet by 4.5 feet.
The 'nap' (fiber direction) of the cloth affects how balls roll and curve, subtly favoring shots hit with the grain.

questions.question: What color is traditional pool table felt?
questions.correctAnswer: Green
questions.explanation: Green felt is the traditional color, tracing back to billiards' roots as a lawn game.

questions.question: A regulation tournament table is roughly what shape?
options: Twice as long as it is wide
Three times as long as wide
questions.correctAnswer: Twice as long as it is wide
questions.explanation: Standard tournament tables use a 2:1 length-to-width ratio, e.g., 9ft x 4.5ft.

questions.question: What does the 'nap' of the cloth refer to?
options: The direction the cloth fibers lie, affecting ball roll
The color pattern of the felt
questions.correctAnswer: The direction the cloth fibers lie, affecting ball roll
questions.explanation: Nap direction can subtly influence how a ball rolls or curves across the table.

facts.text: The rack is the triangular frame used to arrange the balls tightly together before the break shot.
In standard 8-ball, the 8-ball must be placed in the center of the triangle when racking.
A tight rack, with no gaps between balls, is essential for a powerful, evenly-spreading break.

questions.question: What tool is used to arrange the balls before a break?
questions.correctAnswer: The rack
questions.explanation: The rack (often a triangle) holds the balls tightly together for the break shot.

questions.question: In standard 8-ball, where must the 8-ball be placed when racking?
options: At the front of the triangle
In the center of the triangle
questions.correctAnswer: In the center of the triangle
questions.explanation: The 8-ball is placed in the middle row, centered in the triangle.

questions.question: Why is a tight rack (no gaps between balls) important?
options: It produces a more powerful, evenly spread break
It has no real effect on play
questions.correctAnswer: It produces a more powerful, evenly spread break
questions.explanation: Loose racks absorb energy unevenly, leading to weak or lopsided breaks.

facts.text: Standard pool uses 15 numbered balls plus the cue ball: seven solids (1-7), seven stripes (9-15), and the black 8-ball.
A 'combination shot' uses one object ball to strike and pocket another, requiring careful angle calculation.
Advanced players use 'throw' — a slight alteration of a ball's path via friction with the cue ball — to make cuts that look geometrically impossible.

questions.question: How many object balls (excluding the cue ball) are used in standard pool?
questions.explanation: Balls numbered 1-15 make up the full object-ball set.

questions.question: What is a 'combination shot'?
options: Hitting two balls with the cue ball at once
Using one object ball to strike and pocket another
Pocketing two balls in one turn by luck
A shot that requires two players
questions.correctAnswer: Using one object ball to strike and pocket another
questions.explanation: Combos chain the cue ball's energy through one object ball into another.

questions.question: What does 'throw' refer to in advanced shot-making?
options: A ball's path being slightly altered by friction contact with the cue ball
Removing a ball from the table
questions.correctAnswer: A ball's path being slightly altered by friction contact with the cue ball
questions.explanation: Throw is a subtle friction effect that skilled players learn to account for or exploit.

facts.text: The bridge hand supports and guides the cue stick, forming a stable base for the shaft to slide through.
A proper stance — feet shoulder-width apart, aligned with the shot line — keeps the body still so only the arm moves during the stroke.
Consistent cue-ball control depends on a 'pendulum stroke' driven from the elbow, minimizing wrist movement to keep the tip traveling in a straight line.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the bridge hand?
options: To support and guide the cue stick
questions.correctAnswer: To support and guide the cue stick
questions.explanation: The bridge hand forms a stable channel (often a 'V' or loop) that the cue slides through.

questions.question: A proper stance typically involves what body position?
options: Feet shoulder-width apart, aligned with the shot line
Standing as far from the table as possible
questions.correctAnswer: Feet shoulder-width apart, aligned with the shot line
questions.explanation: A balanced, aligned stance keeps the stroke consistent and repeatable.

questions.question: What is a 'pendulum stroke'?
options: A stroke driven mainly from the elbow with minimal wrist movement
A trick shot involving swinging the cue
The motion used only for break shots
questions.correctAnswer: A stroke driven mainly from the elbow with minimal wrist movement
questions.explanation: Pivoting from the elbow like a pendulum keeps the cue's path straight and consistent.
